title: WPI-8 Certificate: Why TWIA Needs It and How to Get One
description: What a WPI-8 certificate is, why TWIA requires windstorm certification in Galveston, and what can happen to your coverage and claim if you do not have one.
html:
If you own property on Galveston Island or along the Texas coast, sooner or later someone will ask whether you have a WPI-8 certificate. Insurance agents ask for it when writing a TWIA policy. Buyers and lenders ask for it at closing. And after a hurricane, it matters again when you replace a roof or rebuild. This article explains what a WPI-8 certificate is, why the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association (TWIA) cares about it, how you get one, and what can happen if your home or your repairs are not certified.

What Is a WPI-8 Certificate?

A WPI-8 is a Certificate of Compliance issued through the Texas Department of Insurance (TDI) windstorm inspection program. It confirms that construction, an addition, or a repair such as a new roof was inspected and found to meet the windstorm building code that applies in the designated catastrophe area, which includes Galveston County and the other first-tier coastal counties.

You may also see the term WPI-8-C. That version is issued based on certification by a TDI-appointed qualified inspector, typically a licensed professional engineer, who inspected the work. For most homeowners, the practical point is the same: the certificate is proof that a specific piece of work was built to the windstorm standard.

A key detail that surprises people: a WPI-8 usually covers a specific scope of work, not the whole house forever. A home can have one certificate for original construction, another for a 2010 addition, and another for a roof replaced after a storm. Each new covered project generally needs its own certification.

Why TWIA Requires Windstorm Certification

TWIA is the insurer of last resort for wind and hail coverage on the Texas coast, and it operates under Texas Insurance Code chapter 2210. To be insurable with TWIA, structures built, altered, remodeled, enlarged or repaired in the catastrophe area are generally required to comply with the applicable windstorm building code, and a certificate of compliance is the standard proof.

In plain terms, TWIA wants evidence that the building can reasonably stand up to coastal wind. The certificate tells them the fasteners, roof deck attachment, shingles or metal panels, straps, openings and other components were installed to the standard.

When You Need a WPI-8 Certificate

  • New construction in the catastrophe area
  • Additions and enlargements, such as a new room, porch enclosure, or garage
  • Roof replacements and many significant roof repairs
  • Window, door and opening replacements that affect the building envelope
  • Structural repairs after hurricane, wind or fire damage
  • Buying or refinancing, when the lender or buyer wants proof the home is insurable with TWIA

Because rules and program details can change, confirm current requirements with TDI, your agent, or a qualified windstorm engineer before work begins. Our Texas windstorm rules page and Galveston local code page summarize the framework that applies here.

How to Get a WPI-8 Certificate Step by Step

  1. Plan before you build or repair. Certification generally depends on inspections during the work, not just at the end. Hire the inspector or engineer before the contractor starts.
  2. Choose a contractor familiar with windstorm work. Ask how many certified jobs they have done in Galveston County and whether they use approved products and fastening schedules.
  3. Schedule the required inspections. For a roof, that often means inspecting deck attachment and underlayment before the covering goes on. If a stage is covered before inspection, you may face expensive tear-off.
  4. Keep product documentation. Save shingle wrappers, product approval information, and invoices. Manufacturer wind ratings matter; see our shingle wind calculators for how rated wind speeds compare.
  5. Get the final certification filed. After the work is complete and compliant, the inspector submits the paperwork and the certificate is issued.
  6. Store copies safely. Keep a digital copy off-site. After a hurricane, you do not want to be digging through a flooded filing cabinet.

What Happens Without a WPI-8 Certificate

Coverage problems

Without proof of compliance, TWIA may decline to issue or renew coverage on the structure or on the uncertified addition. Some owners discover this only when they try to renew or sell. Depending on the circumstances, there may be options to obtain a certificate after the fact, but that can require an engineer's evaluation and sometimes opening up finished work.

Claim complications

If a storm damages part of the home that was never certified, it can complicate the claim. Coverage questions about an uncertified addition, for example, can slow things down. Understanding exactly which parts of your home are certified is important before you file a TWIA windstorm claim.

Sale and financing delays

Lenders on the coast typically require wind coverage. If the home cannot get it, closings can stall. Buyers increasingly ask for WPI-8 copies during due diligence.

The WPI-8 Certificate and Your Insurance Claim

This is where many Galveston homeowners miss money. When a storm damages your roof or structure, the repairs generally must meet the current windstorm code and be certified. That can add real cost:

  • Engineer or inspector fees for certification
  • Upgraded fastening and nailing patterns
  • Additional roof deck attachment or re-nailing
  • Code-required underlayment and flashing
  • Hurricane straps or connectors where required
  • Impact-rated or wind-rated openings where required

Whether those costs are paid depends on your policy wording, including any building ordinance or law coverage. Do not assume the insurer's estimate includes them. Compare the estimate line by line against what your contractor and engineer say the certified repair will actually require. If the carrier's scope would not pass a windstorm inspection, that gap is worth raising in writing.

Also keep the claim timeline in mind. TWIA claims must be reported within one year of the date of loss, and waiting on certification questions is not a reason to delay reporting the damage.

WPI-8 Certificate Checklist for Galveston Owners

  • Find copies of every WPI-8 or WPI-8-C tied to your property
  • List which parts of the home each certificate covers
  • Identify any additions or repairs done without certification
  • Before any repair, line up a qualified inspector first
  • Keep product labels, approvals and invoices
  • After a storm, include certification costs in your claim documentation
  • Store digital copies somewhere safe from flood and wind

How a Public Adjuster Can Help

A licensed public adjuster, licensed in Texas by TDI, represents you rather than the insurer. On a coastal wind claim, that includes reviewing whether the insurer's estimate reflects a repair that can actually be certified, documenting code-related costs, and making sure the claim is presented with the right support. We cannot promise any result, but we can make sure the certification issue is not overlooked.

faq.q: Does a WPI-8 certificate cover my whole house?
faq.a: Not necessarily. A WPI-8 generally certifies a specific scope of work, such as original construction, an addition, or a roof replacement. Many coastal homes have several certificates for different projects.

faq.q: Can I get a WPI-8 certificate after the work is done?
faq.a: Sometimes, but it can be difficult and expensive because inspections are normally done during construction. An engineer may need to evaluate the work and parts of it may need to be exposed. Check with a qualified windstorm engineer and TDI.

faq.q: Will my insurance claim pay for windstorm certification costs?
faq.a: It depends on your policy wording, including any ordinance or law coverage. Review your policy and compare the insurer's estimate with what a certified repair will actually require.
